event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: COVID-19 is referenced in EOG’s 2024 Form 10-K primarily as a medium-term, lingering headwind rather than an acute crisis.  The company acknowledges that pandemic-related conditions have already had operational and cost impacts—most notably through supply-chain bottlenecks, inflationary pressures and labour shortages—and flags the disease as an ongoing macro driver of commodity-price volatility.  These remarks are recent enough (≈4 years after the WHO declaration) to avoid heavy time-decay discounts, yet are framed mostly in qualitative language with no quantified dollar hit or forward guidance.  Accordingly, the pandemic is presented as a material but manageable risk: it has produced actual cost inflation and could still influence prices and logistics, but mitigation efforts and the fading intensity of the outbreak temper severity.  Under the Time Decay Principle (4-10-year window), individual evidence snippets therefore merit moderate scores (roughly 4-6 for direct impacts; lower where discussion is generic), yielding an overall medium-level risk assessment.

evidence_list.snippet: • the duration and economic and financial impact of epidemics, pandemics or other public health issues, such as the COVID-19 pandemic;

components.reason: Explicitly cites the COVID-19 pandemic as a factor that can affect commodity-price volatility, directly tying the event to business risk.
Statement is forward-looking and generic (‘can or could cause’), with no company-specific metrics or demonstrated impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: The sentence directly links COVID-19 to potential financial impacts but remains high-level and hypothetical, so it receives a low-moderate score of 1.

evidence_list.snippet: Such inflationary pressures on our operating costs and capital expenditures resulted from (i) supply chain disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and the resulting limited availability of certain materials and products manufactured using such materials; (ii) increased demand for fuel and steel; (iii) increased demand for drilling and completion services coupled with a limited number of available service providers, resulting in increased competition for such services among EOG and other companies in its industry; (iv) labor shortages; and (v) other factors, including the ongoing conflict between Russia and the Ukraine which began in late February 2022.

components.reason: Attributes experienced cost inflation directly to supply-chain disruptions caused by COVID-19, demonstrating an actual realized impact.
Identifies specific operational areas affected—operating costs, capital expenditures, supply chain, labour—indicating breadth of effect.
No numeric quantification of the dollar magnitude and notes the pressures have diminished, slightly mitigating severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Because it links real inflationary cost impacts to COVID-19 across multiple operational domains, but without quantification, the snippet earns a medium-high score of 5, consistent with a 4-year-old event.
